candidates.title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
candidates.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools. However, malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations can manipulate their decisions and induce unsafe actions. Adversarial co-evolution has emerged as an effective approach to strengthening LLM safety, but existing work primarily focuses on language-level safety or indirect prompt injection in web tasks. In this paper, we introduce AgentSafeEvo, a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework for agent safety built on an attacker-defender game spanning diverse tasks and attack types. candidates.title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
candidates.summary: Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based web agents provide practical, high-precision solutions for visual browser automation; however, they inherently expand the attack surface, introducing novel vision-based vulnerabilities. Existing adversarial evaluations targeting these agents frequently rely on permissive threat models and visually conspicuous artifacts. In this paper, we investigate a constrained vulnerability detection setting: a trusted web platform where the evaluator acts solely as an unprivileged third party, such as a merchant or advertiser, controlling only a semantically legitimate, spatially constrained region, such as an ad slot, a sponsored card, or a localized widget.

candidates.title: Constraining Tool Authority in AI Agents: A Risk-Tiered Framework for Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection
candidates.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
candidates.summary: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents read untrusted content, such as emails, web pages, and documents, and act through tools. Instructions hidden in that content can steer the agent, and the agent's permissions can turn that influence into unauthorized actions. This paper proposes a risk-based authorization architecture that reduces the consequences of indirect prompt injection without assuming the model resists it. candidates.title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
candidates.summary: LLM-based agents increasingly execute long-horizon, end-to-end workflows involving shell commands, code modification, dependency installation, and interaction with remote services. candidates.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
candidates.summary: Tool-using agents read untrusted external content, which exposes them to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where hidden instructions hijack the agent's tool calls. Benchmarks measure IPI security by the attack success rate (ASR), which treats every failed attack as a successful defense. candidates.summary: With the rapid integration of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into real-world applications, Prompt Injection (PI) has emerged as a critical security threat. candidates.title: THE DUAL ROLE OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN CYBERSECURITY: THREATS, DEFENSES, AND RESEARCH DIRECTIONS
candidates.venue: “ADVANCED JOURNAL OF UNIVERSITY SCIENCE AND CREATIVE INNOVATIONS” AJOU SCI
candidates.summary: Large language models (LLMs), have come in from three angles into the cybersecurity world. They're a new class of system that has to be secured, they are a capability that reduces the cost of offense, and they are a tool that enhances defense. Current reviews consider either of these directions only, making it hard for researchers and practitioners to glimpse the interplay of the three. This review collates research published from 2023–2026 in all three of the following, presented in the dual-use approach. candidates.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
candidates.summary: Modern LLM agents persist state across sessions via two channels: long-lived memory files silently prepended to the system prompt, and scheduled tasks waking the agent without user input. A one-time indirect prompt injection committed to either channel can re-fire across sessions long after the attacker leaves, threats we term carryover attacks. Existing prompt-injection benchmarks evaluate attacks only in the session where malicious content is first observed, leaving the gate governing when and how often a planted payload later re-fires unmeasured. candidates.title: Agentic AI Architectures: A Survey of Patterns, Memory Systems, and Protocols
candidates.summary: AI agents have grown dramatically more capable — planning over futures, calling tools, remembering across sessions, coordinating in teams — while the data they act upon remains ungoverned, untested, and uninspected. This survey argues that AI agents are as good as their data foundations: an agent’s capability ceiling in production is set not by its language model but by the quality, governance, freshness, and semantic structure of the data it perceives and acts upon. candidates.title: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents
candidates.summary: Browser agents automate complex workflows by reading and acting on arbitrary page content, but this flexibility exposes them to prompt injection attacks and unintended data exfiltration. candidates.title: TRACER: Trace-Regularized Training Against Indirect Prompt Injection
candidates.summary: Indirect prompt injection uses untrusted retrieved content, tool outputs, or agent messages to override an LLM's intended behavior. We show that defense robustness is channel-conditioned: the same attack succeeds 18% of the time as a follow-up message but 53% when placed in retrieved context. We propose TRACER (Trace-Regularized Adversarial Channel Exposure with Reward-shaping), a channel-aware adversarial training method that samples presentation wrappers and combines an answer-anchored, evidence-gated reward with ATRC, which aligns attacked reasoning with clean evidence when an injection is invalid. candidates.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
candidates.summary: An independent, fully-local red-team study of indirect prompt injection against a reconstructed GitHub issue-triage agent. Across 712 logged agent runs on 9 models spanning three capability tiers (weak, mid, frontier), the study records 49 verified credential leaks, using a synthetic canary as the exfiltration target. Results are sharply tiered: weak and mid models leak readily, while frontier models hold. The mechanism is a split between two steps. candidates.title: Prompt-Injection Probes Learn the Conversation, Not Just the Injection
candidates.summary: Linear probes on a model's hidden states are used as cheap monitors for indirect prompt injection: they screen the tool outputs an agent reads and send suspicious ones to a slower second check, so every false alarm has a cost. candidates.summary: AI agents that operate a web browser on a user's behalf routinely stall at login pages. The usual workarounds each have a cost. candidates.summary: This paper studies the problem of safe tool execution for large language model (LLM) agents under prompt injection.
